topStories.headline: Ohio State Highway Patrol Investigating Fatal Crash That Killed Caledonia Man
topStories.dek: James R. Schilling III, 41, died October 30 when his pickup left a rural Marion County road and overturned; the case remains under investigation.
topStories.body:
The Ohio State Highway Patrol's Marion Post is investigating a fatal single-vehicle crash on Township Road 10 near Township Road 71 in Marion County. James R. Schilling III, 41, of Caledonia, died after his pickup truck left the roadway, struck a tree, and rolled over multiple times. Troopers were dispatched to the scene at approximately 6:10 p.m. on October 30, according to Marion County Now.

No other vehicles were involved, and the patrol has not released information about contributing factors. The investigation remains open and no charges have been announced.

The crash is among a series of fatal collisions investigated by the Marion Post on rural roads in Marion County in recent months. The patrol's Marion Post handles crashes across the county, including roads running through the Caledonia and surrounding township areas.

topStories.headline: Marion County Split With Ohio on Top Statewide Races; Local Offices Largely Uncontested
topStories.dek: County voters backed Ramaswamy for governor and Husted for U.S. Senate on November 3, while both races went the other way statewide.
topStories.body:
Marion County cast its ballots differently from the statewide majority in the two marquee contests of the November 3 general election. Republican Vivek Ramaswamy carried the county in the race for Ohio governor even as Democrat Amy Acton won statewide by about eight percentage points — the first Democratic gubernatorial victory in Ohio since 2006. Republican Jon Husted similarly won Marion County in the U.S. Senate contest while Democrat Sherrod Brown prevailed statewide.

In the 4th Congressional District, which covers Marion County, Republican incumbent Jim Jordan won re-election with 64.49 percent of the county vote to Democrat Joshua D. Kolasinski's 31.25 percent. In Ohio House District 86, Republican Ben Weber defeated Democrat Kent Halloran 59.20 percent to 40.80 percent in the county.

Several local races were uncontested. Republican Kenneth H. Stiverson was elected Marion County Commissioner without opposition, as was Democrat Joan Kasotis in a separate commissioner seat. Republican Timothy F. Garner was returned as Marion County Coroner unopposed. Levy renewal measures for Elgin Local Schools, at 2.88 mills over five years, and Ridgedale Local Schools, at 2.44 mills over five years, also appeared on the ballot.

topStories.headline: Marion City Council to Meet November 23 as Year-End Budget Deadline Approaches
topStories.dek: The next regular council session is scheduled for Monday evening at City Hall, with fiscal year 2026 finances among the ongoing items before the body.
topStories.body:
Marion City Council holds its next regular meeting on Monday, November 23, at Marion City Hall, 233 W. Center Street. The city's online calendar lists the session; agendas are posted to the city's Agenda Center at least 24 hours before each meeting, per city practice.

The November sitting comes as the council continues work on the city's budget for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2026. Committee documents from earlier in the year show Finance Committee members tracking budget performance reports, revenue worksheets, and an appropriations ordinance for state-required police training among the financial matters pending before the full council.

City Hall will close Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. Residents with questions about the November 23 agenda can reach the Clerk of Council's office at 740-387-4935.

moreNews.headline: City Curbside Leaf Collection Continues Through Fall
moreNews.body: Mayor Bill Collins announced in October that Marion's annual curbside leaf collection program is underway for city residents. Leaves should be raked to the curb; no bags are required for the city-run collection. The program runs through the fall season.

moreNews.headline: Marion Palace Theatre Lines Up Full December Holiday Schedule
moreNews.body: Following the Sara Evans concert this week, the Marion Palace Theatre has a packed December calendar. Upcoming events include National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation on December 11, a White Christmas Sing-Along on December 12, Sounds of the Season on December 13, and The Muppet Christmas Carol on December 19, in addition to the three-night Christmas at the Palace run December 4–6.
